briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for July 26, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensification of Extreme Climate Events Worldwide
sections.content: Today, extreme weather events continue to cause damage and raise concerns across the globe. In the Western United States, climate change has made snow droughts approximately four times more likely, and Canadian wildfire smoke is also being attributed to the impacts of climate change [7, 8]. Across Europe, climate change is 'supercharging' droughts and exacerbating the situation, with emergency situations arising in France and Spain where over 250,000 people have been evacuated due to large-scale wildfires [9, 15, 18, 19]. Furthermore, health threats related to heatwaves are escalating, with a third 'heat dome' in a month expected to hit 70 million people in the U.S., and 'covert heatstroke,' where mental clarity is affected even without outdoor activity, being warned as particularly dangerous for the elderly in Japan [5, 17]. Monsoon diseases are also frequently misdiagnosed due to similar symptoms and diagnostic gaps, illustrating the complexity of health issues caused by climate change [13].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Persistent Domestic Heatwaves and Carbon Neutral Infrastructure Challenges
sections.content: Domestically, heatwave advisories are expected to continue across most regions tomorrow (the 26th), with sweltering heat persisting. Showers are forecast mainly for the central region, but 'steaming heat' and tropical nights are expected to continue for the time being [6]. Amidst these extreme climate conditions, South Korea's adoption rate of heat pumps, considered a key infrastructure for the carbon-neutral era, remains low, raising concerns [2]. This remains a critical challenge for enhancing energy efficiency and achieving greenhouse gas reduction targets [2].

sections.title: 🌱 Exploring Climate Change Adaptation and Eco-Friendly Solutions
sections.content: Even amidst this climate crisis, positive developments and innovative attempts to adapt to and address climate change are being observed. The Robert Mondavi Winery, reopening after three years, presented a vision for the future of agriculture in the face of climate change, armed with organic practices, advanced winemaking, and precision harvesting technologies [1]. As international oil prices surpassed $100, renewable energy ETFs showed strength, reflecting market anticipation for a shift towards eco-friendly energy [3]. Furthermore, the French company Momentum Technologies unveiled a mobile survival capsule designed for disaster situations such as terrorism and floods. Discussions on how to construct highways in the era of climate change, along with the spotlight on nature-based solutions, demonstrate ongoing efforts across various sectors to seek adaptation and solutions [4, 10, 11]. The lifting of the major wildfire threat in Scotland's Cairngorms National Park, allowing evacuated residents to return home, is also positive news [16].

sections.title: 🌍 Widespread Impacts Caused by Climate Change
sections.content: Climate change extends beyond mere weather patterns, exerting widespread impacts across the Earth's fundamental systems and ecosystems. Scientists have revealed that climate change is gradually lengthening the Earth's day, and ecosystem disruptions are intensifying, such as the imbalance in the wetland habitats of Painted Storks [12, 14]. Meanwhile, fossil fuel-related projects are also experiencing setbacks, with a new North Sea oil drilling project facing delays due to an offshore equipment drop accident [20]. These reports once again serve as a reminder that climate change is affecting human life, the natural environment, and industries in unexpected ways [12, 14, 20].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights the global intensification of extreme weather events, alongside innovative efforts to address them. Understanding the extensive impacts of climate change and committing to continuous adaptation and mitigation efforts is of paramount importance. This concludes today's climate briefing.

articles.title: Often Mistaken for a Cold... 'Stealth Heatstroke' Signals One Doesn't Even Realize
articles.description: An illustration related to heatstroke. Kyunghyang Shinmun archive photo. Individuals may not experience severe thirst or prolonged outdoor activity, yet suddenly find their minds clouded and speech slurred. The critical issue is the lack of self-awareness regarding heatstroke. The medical community warns that this 'unnoticed heatstroke,' particularly prevalent among the elderly, represents a significant summer health risk. In Japan, currently experiencing severe heatwaves, this phenomenon is a growing concern.

summary.phenomenon: In Japan, where extreme heatwaves have recently continued, 'stealth heatstroke,' which progresses without the individual's awareness, is being warned as a particularly dangerous type among the elderly. This form of heatstroke manifests with symptoms such as mental confusion and slurred speech, even without severe thirst or prolonged outdoor activity.
summary.outlook: The medical community is warning that 'unnoticed heatstroke' among the elderly is one of the dangerous types during the summer season.
